subject.title: fix(infra): release exec-approvals locks across VirtioFS identity drift

question: Should OpenClaw ship this local exec-approvals lock protocol, adopt an upstream `@openclaw/fs-safe` repair, or retain the earlier OpenClaw implementation as the single canonical fix?
rationale: All three paths modify the same authorization-store lock invariant, and choosing the permanent ownership boundary is a security and maintenance decision that source-level review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Pause for a canonical lock-owner decision
options.body: Review this PR, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028, and https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/45 together, then choose one implementation and recovery contract before merging any of them.

options.title: Adopt this PR as the local fix
options.body: Keep the fix scoped to exec approvals, close or supersede the competing OpenClaw PR, and require current-head VirtioFS proof before merge.

options.title: Move the repair upstream
options.body: Wait for a reviewed `@openclaw/fs-safe` release, update OpenClaw to consume it, and prove that the dependency preserves exec-approval fail-closed behavior.

recommendation.title: Pause for a canonical lock-owner decision
recommendation.body: Review this PR, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028, and https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/pull/45 together, then choose one implementation and recovery contract before merging any of them.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor introduced the nonce ownership and async-path implementation lineage that the maintainer must either retain, replace, or move upstream.
